classification_signals: The paper presents arguments and propositions about the relationship between architecture, patterns, and mathematics, rather than reporting new empirical data.
It synthesizes historical context, psychological insights, and architectural theory to build a conceptual framework.
Sections like 'Introduction', 'A science of patterns', 'Architectural counter-arguments', and 'A mathematical template for our environment' are characteristic of theoretical discourse.
The author's 'About the author' section mentions his theoretical results and application of complex physical systems to architecture, aligning with a theoretical paper.
title: Architecture, Patterns, and Mathematics

findings.antecedent: suppression of pattern in modernist architecture
findings.consequent: impoverished man's experience of both mathematics and the built environment
findings.quote: The modernist movement suppresses pattern in architecture, and this has profound implications for society as a whole.

findings.antecedent: presence or absence of patterns in our surroundings
findings.consequent: ease of grasping concepts that rely on patterns (mathematics)
findings.quote: the presence or absence of patterns in our surroundings influences how easily one is able to grasp concepts that rely on patterns.

findings.antecedent: elimination of patterns from twentieth-century architecture
findings.consequent: capacity to process and interpret patterns in thought
findings.quote: Eliminating patterns from twentieth-century architecture affects our capacity to process and interpret patterns in thought.

findings.antecedent: environmental factor (pattern-less world)
findings.consequent: overall decline of mathematics in society (declining mathematical capacity among students)
findings.quote: an environmental factor might contribute to the overall decline of mathematics in our society.

findings.antecedent: traditional architectures obeying intrinsically mathematical rules [1,2]
findings.consequent: buildings encapsulating multiple mathematical qualities and information
findings.quote: traditional architectures obey rules that are intrinsically mathematical [1,2]. Those rules lead to buildings that... encapsulate... multiple mathematical qualities and information.

findings.antecedent: architecture of the twentieth century
findings.consequent: novelty and a break with the past by eliminating mathematical qualities
findings.quote: The architecture of the twentieth century has achieved novelty, and a break with the past, precisely by eliminating those qualities.

findings.antecedent: ordered mathematical information in the environment
findings.consequent: positive emotional responses
findings.quote: Ordered mathematical information in the environment generates positive emotional responses.

findings.antecedent: environment that is implicitly anti-mathematical
findings.consequent: interest in mathematics; ability to grasp mathematical concepts
findings.quote: If we are raised in an environment that is implicitly anti-mathematical, that adversely affects our interest in mathematics; possibly even our ability to grasp mathematical concepts.

findings.antecedent: spending one's whole life in a pattern-less world
findings.consequent: crucial capacity to form patterns
findings.quote: Does spending one's whole life in a pattern-less world weaken or even destroy the crucial capacity to form patterns?

findings.antecedent: patterns in the mind mimicking patterns in nature and man-made patterns
findings.consequent: human ability to do mathematics
findings.quote: Patterns in the mind mimic patterns in nature as well as man-made patterns, which is probably how human beings evolved so as to be able to do mathematics.

findings.antecedent: basic inner need to externalize connective structures generated in the mind via thinking
findings.consequent: ubiquitousness of visual patterns in traditional art and architecture
findings.quote: Mankind generates patterns out of some basic inner need: it externalizes connective structures generated in the mind via the process of thinking, which explains the ubiquitousness of visual patterns in the traditional art and architecture of mankind.

findings.antecedent: patterns in time (natural rhythms, annual events, repeating gestures, rhythmic patterns in voice/music)
findings.consequent: human intellectual development
findings.quote: Patterns in time are also essential to human intellectual development.

findings.antecedent: organized complexity in physical and chemical systems (self-organization)
findings.consequent: perceivable patterns on a macroscopic scale
findings.quote: The system's organized complexity is manifested on a macroscopic scale as perceivable patterns.

findings.antecedent: architectural patterns (tilings, visual patterns)
findings.consequent: primary contact with mathematics for many people before mass education
findings.quote: architectural patterns represent one of the few primary contacts with mathematics.

findings.antecedent: patterns in the visual environment of a developing child
findings.consequent: innate creative ability and talent for mathematics
findings.quote: The necessity for patterns in the visual environment of a developing child is acknowledged by child psychologists as being highly instrumental.

findings.antecedent: elimination of visual patterns
findings.consequent: mind set valuing only unique, irreproducible cases; elimination of all patterns (visual and in solution space)
findings.source: Alexandrine patterns as inherited architectural solutions
findings.quote: The elimination of visual patterns... creates a mind set that values only unique, irreproducible cases; that has the consequence of eliminating all patterns, visual ones as well as those occurring in solution space.

findings.antecedent: traditional architectural patterns (which work well)
findings.consequent: avoidance by blocking the deductive process relating effect with cause
findings.quote: The only way to avoid coming back to traditional architectural patterns which work so well - is to block the deductive process that relates an effect with its cause.

findings.antecedent: deliberately ignoring consequences of design decisions
findings.consequent: architectural and urban mistakes repeated with disastrous consequences
findings.quote: By deliberately ignoring the consequences of design decisions, architectural and urban mistakes are repeated over and over again, with the same disastrous consequences each time.

findings.antecedent: loss of literacy during the middle ages
findings.consequent: loss of visual or architectural patterns
findings.quote: The regrettable loss of literacy during those centuries was most emphatically not accompanied by a commensurate loss of visual or architectural patterns, because patterns (as opposed to the abstract representations of a written script) reflect processes that are inherent in the human mind.

findings.antecedent: elimination of ornament (Modernist design canon)
findings.consequent: removal of all ordered structural differentiations from 5mm to 2m scales (human scale)
findings.quote: The elimination of ornament removes all ordered structural differentiations from the range of scales 5mm to 2m or thereabouts.

findings.antecedent: Modernist design canon (patterns cannot be defined on human scales)
findings.consequent: removal of mathematical information from the built environment
findings.quote: In the Modernist design canon, patterns cannot be defined on those scales. Therefore, modernism removes mathematical information from the built environment.

findings.antecedent: visual patterns (on building façades, walls, pavements)
findings.consequent: strongest emotional and cognitive impact on human beings (due to immediate accessibility)
findings.quote: Visual patterns have the strongest emotional and cognitive impact when they are immediately accessible.

findings.antecedent: use of proportional ratios (e.g., Golden Mean, 5:3, 8:5, √2)
findings.consequent: subdivision of forms to define coincident scales; positive effect
findings.quote: What actually occurs is that the use of proportional ratios often also subdivides forms so as to define coincident scales, and this has a strongly positive effect.

findings.antecedent: Modernist architecture (proposing pure geometric solids as 'mathematical')
findings.consequent: simplistic mathematical basis
findings.quote: Proposing pure geometric solids as "mathematical" is totally simplistic.

findings.antecedent: hierarchy reversal (building structures on a large scale that are natural only on the small scale)
findings.consequent: structures appearing out of place and novel (e.g., giant pyramids, rectangular boxes)
findings.quote: One of these is hierarchy reversal: "build structures on a large scale that are natural only on the small scale; they then appear out of place, and therefore novel."

findings.antecedent: Modernist city planning (imposing simplistic geometry on city form)
findings.consequent: rich mathematical complexity of the urban environment
findings.quote: by imposing a simplistic geometry on city form, post-war planning drastically reduces the rich mathematical complexity of the urban environment [16,17].

findings.antecedent: hierarchy reversal in modernist buildings and streets
findings.consequent: monotonous patterns visible only from an airplane
findings.quote: With hierarchy reversal, the monotonous patterns defined by modernist buildings and streets are visible only from an airplane.

findings.antecedent: removal of essential patterns (spatial and dynamical) from historical cities by urbanists
findings.consequent: creation of empty suburbia and monstrous office buildings
findings.quote: They removed the essential patterns (not only the spatial ones, but more importantly, the dynamical ones) present in the great historical cities, to create empty suburbia and monstrous office buildings.

findings.antecedent: natural materials
findings.consequent: embodiment of organized complexity below 5mm, providing mathematical information to viewer through microscopic surface structure
findings.quote: Natural materials embody organized complexity in the scales below 5mm, and thereby provide mathematical information to a viewer through their microscopic surface structure.

findings.antecedent: mathematically deficient design + use of expensive materials (Modernist architects)
findings.consequent: emotionally uncomfortable buildings; camouflage of design deficiencies
findings.quote: Emotionally uncomfortable buildings... camouflage a mathematically deficient design through the use of expensive materials.

findings.antecedent: Modernist architecture (explicit stylistic dictate)
findings.consequent: fractal properties; unnatural appearance
findings.source: Classical and modern mathematics: is there an architectural analogy?
findings.quote: By explicit stylistic dictate, modernist architecture has no fractal properties, and that is one reason why it appears unnatural [20].

findings.antecedent: traditional architecture (including Classical style)
findings.consequent: explicitly fractal properties (fractal subdivisions and scaling)
findings.source: Classical and modern mathematics: is there an architectural analogy?
findings.quote: Traditional architecture, on the other hand, including that in a Classical style, tends to be explicitly fractal.

findings.antecedent: Modernist architecture (simplistic rectangular forms)
findings.consequent: very little mathematical content
findings.source: Classical and modern mathematics: is there an architectural analogy?
findings.quote: The simplistic vocabulary of rectangular Modernist forms has very little mathematical content.

findings.antecedent: Modernism
findings.consequent: removal of fractals from our environment
findings.quote: Modernism removes fractals from our environment.

findings.antecedent: pure Platonic solids
findings.consequent: incompatibility with fractals (exist only on a single level of scale)
findings.quote: Pure Platonic solids and fractals are incompatible, because the former exist only on a single level of scale.

findings.antecedent: buildings of Le Corbusier and Mies van der Rohe (intentional violation of fractal rules [1,2])
findings.consequent: distinction from natural forms and traditional building styles
findings.quote: The buildings of Le Corbusier and Mies van der Rohe intentionally violate this rule, in an attempt to distinguish themselves both from natural forms, and from traditional building styles [1,2].

findings.antecedent: Frank Lloyd Wright's buildings
findings.consequent: self-similar characteristic over a wide range of scales (intrinsically fractal)
findings.quote: Frank Lloyd Wright's buildings display a self-similar characteristic over a wide range of scales, from a distant view to finger-tip size detail, so those buildings are intrinsically fractal.

findings.antecedent: Le Corbusier's architecture
findings.consequent: self-similar characteristic over only two or three largest scales; flat and straight up close (no fractal qualities)
findings.quote: Le Corbusier's architecture displays a self-similar characteristic over only two or three of the largest scales... Up close, Le Corbusier's architecture is flat and straight, and therefore has no fractal qualities.

findings.antecedent: deconstructivist buildings (unbalanced, chaotic forms)
findings.consequent: randomness; lack of patterns on single or multiple scales
findings.quote: deconstructivist buildings have only led to randomness.

findings.antecedent: contemporary buildings (decoration minimal/invisible or intentionally disarrayed/broken)
findings.consequent: incoherence; avoidance of organized complexity
findings.quote: Any decoration appearing on contemporary buildings is either so minimal as to be hardly visible, or it is intentionally disarrayed and broken so that it is incoherent.

findings.antecedent: built environment of recent decades (eliminating ordered, fractal structures; replacing with empty rectangles, planes, chaotic forms)
findings.consequent: strong message that complex patterns are not allowed; subconscious learning that such objects are 'not modern'
findings.source: A mathematical template for our environment
findings.quote: This provides a strong message that complex patterns are not allowed as part of our contemporary world. Subconsciously, people learn that such objects are “not modern”...

findings.antecedent: civilization turning against structures with organized complexity (animate and inanimate)
findings.consequent: elimination of mathematical information from our environment; reversal of mathematical values
findings.source: A mathematical template for our environment
findings.quote: Our civilization has turned against those structures, animate as well as inanimate, that possess organized complexity. We are taught by our schools and media to eliminate mathematical information from our environment.

findings.antecedent: chaotic forms (too much internally uncoordinated information)
findings.consequent: overload of the mind's capacity to process information
findings.quote: Chaotic forms, however, have too much internally uncoordinated information, so that they overload the mind's capacity to process information.

findings.antecedent: random information (failing to correlate)
findings.consequent: incoherence; inability to encode
findings.quote: Random information is incoherent: by failing to correlate, it cannot be encoded [25].

findings.antecedent: monotonous repetition without subsymmetries (minimal pattern on single scale)
findings.consequent: little information content
findings.quote: At the empty (modernist) extreme, monotonous repetition provides little information, although if it does contain any, it is well organized.

findings.antecedent: Modernism (very repetitive designs, applied to large scales, avoided in human-scale)
findings.consequent: elimination of complexity and information; simplification of built environment; diminished impact as observable pattern
findings.quote: Modernism uses very repetitive designs as a way of eliminating complexity and information, thereby simplifying the built environment. Moreover, repetition is always applied to the large scales, and avoided in the small (i.e., human) range of scales, which further diminishes its impact as an observable pattern.

findings.antecedent: patterned floor tiling (connecting to pedestrian through information)
findings.consequent: space made more immediate and useful; support for ancillary building functions
findings.quote: By connecting to the pedestrian through information, the space is made more immediate -- hence, more useful -- and at the same time it supports any ancillary functions of the whole building.

findings.antecedent: architecture (ubiquitous, embodying ideas)
findings.consequent: influence on everyday life and way of thinking
findings.quote: As architecture is ubiquitous, the ideas it embodies influence our everyday life and way of thinking to a remarkable extent.

findings.antecedent: training people to reject mathematical information in the built environment
findings.consequent: reversal of mathematical values; pervasive aesthetic
findings.quote: We have trained people to reject mathematical information in the built environment. This reversal of mathematical values not only applies to buildings and urban regions; it defines a pervasive aesthetic.

limitations: The definitive answer to the question of whether a pattern-less world weakens the capacity to form patterns is not known.
The paper is a theoretical proposition and calls for further investigation into the relationship between architecture and mathematics.
minimum_safe_summary: This theoretical paper argues that the suppression of patterns in 20th-century modernist architecture has negatively impacted human intellectual development, particularly mathematical capacity, by removing essential mathematical information from the built environment. Historically, architecture and mathematics were intertwined, with traditional designs embodying complex, organized patterns across scales. Modernist and deconstructivist styles, however, prioritize empty, random, or overly simplistic forms, leading to an 'anti-mathematical mind-set' and a decline in the ability to process and interpret patterns. The author proposes that a return to organized complexity in design is crucial for human cognitive and emotional well-being, noting that the definitive answer to the question of pattern-less environments weakening cognitive capacity is not yet known and requires further investigation.
